title: Create final milestone and acceptance verification gate
description:
Problem statement:
Create a final acceptance gate that maps every plan acceptance criterion and milestone to tests, manual checks, or explicit documented evidence.

Source-plan context:
- JOPLIN-MCP-RUST.md:2036-2056 Milestone 1 local proof: server starts, migrations, schema check fixture, fake Joplin auth bootstrap, token minted/stored hashed, HMAC key validation, notes index fixture, search note, list tag, VictoriaLogs logs, test polls logs. No real Joplin required.
- JOPLIN-MCP-RUST.md:2058-2081 Milestone 2 real Joplin DB: read users, authenticate, SOPS test credentials, resolve user_id, email refresh, session invalidation, build index, compare note, encrypted skipped, another user invisible, soft/hard deletes, tag filters, logs.
- JOPLIN-MCP-RUST.md:2083-2103 Milestone 3 harness usability: client bootstrap/serve, harness config, status/list/get/search/change/logout tools.
- JOPLIN-MCP-RUST.md:1800-1853 required build/test command contract, including required Justfile aliases, required `tests/compose.local.yaml`, and live `http://victorialogs.lan:9428` endpoint.
- JOPLIN-MCP-RUST.md:2105-2140 acceptance criteria list.

Scope:
- Add an acceptance checklist document or test metadata mapping each criterion to verification.
- Ensure every issue in this tree has a path into final acceptance.
- Identify any remaining manual checks clearly.
- Add a CI/local command summary for running Milestone 1 and non-secret tests.
- Include the exact stable command set: cargo fmt/clippy/build/test, nix flake check/build, `just test-all-local`, and `JP_MCP_LIVE_JOPLIN=1 just test-real-joplin`.
- Include evidence that local tests use `tests/compose.local.yaml`.
- Include evidence that live-Joplin tests use separate Joplin and MCP databases.
- Include evidence that live-Joplin tests use `http://victorialogs.lan:9428`.

Out of scope:
- Do not implement missing features here; file follow-up if a criterion has no owner.
- Do not require real-Joplin credentials for default acceptance unless explicitly enabled.

Desired outcome:
The final executor can tell when JP-MCP v1 is actually done without rereading the entire plan.

Verification:
- Every acceptance criterion has a test/manual evidence mapping.
- Every milestone deliverable has an owner issue or completed evidence.
- Running the documented acceptance gate gives clear pass/fail output.
- Default local acceptance does not decrypt `secrets.yaml`.
- Live acceptance requires `JP_MCP_LIVE_JOPLIN=1`, proves `joplin_database != mcp_database`, and uses `http://victorialogs.lan:9428`.
notes: Confirmed build/test and DB contract: SOPS test keys are .joplin.url, .joplin.username, .joplin.password, plus .postgres.host, .postgres.port, .postgres.joplin_database, .postgres.joplin_user, .postgres.joplin_password, .postgres.mcp_database, .postgres.mcp_user, and .postgres.mcp_password. postgres.joplin_database is the canonical Joplin Server database and must be accessed with postgres.joplin_user read-only. postgres.mcp_database is the separate MCP database and must be accessed with postgres.mcp_user for joplin_mcp schema, migrations, tokens, audit log, and derived indexes. Integration/e2e credential use must be explicit opt-in; dry-run checks may report key-name presence only; never print/log/snapshot/panic with decrypted values, DSNs, passwords, tokens, or generated configs containing them. Justfile is the required command surface. tests/compose.local.yaml is the required local service runner for disposable Postgres, fake Joplin auth, and local VictoriaLogs. Live tests use JP_MCP_LIVE_JOPLIN=1 just test-real-joplin and must use http://victorialogs.lan:9428 for VictoriaLogs ingestion and queries.

title: Implement test-id propagation and VictoriaLogs polling test harness
description:

- Implement VictoriaLogs query client for tests.

- Provide assertions for expected log events.

- Live-Joplin tests use `http://victorialogs.lan:9428`.

title: Complete client bootstrap, status, logout, serve proxy, and test-id forwarding
description:

  - Unsupported version returns 400 Bad Request.
  - Omitted header outside initialization is unsupported.

title: Implement MCP token generation, HMAC storage, expiry, and revocation
description:
Problem statement:
Implement MCP token generation, HMAC hashing, storage, expiry, rotation support, lookup, revocation, and safe request context attachment.

Source-plan context:
- JOPLIN-MCP-RUST.md:594-651 defines token model:
  - Raw token format `mcp_<base64url random bytes>`.
  - Generate at least 32 random bytes before base64url encoding.
  - Never store raw token; store keyed HMAC.
  - Store hmac_key_id with each token row.
  - Default token expiry 90 days; non-expiring tokens require config and explicit CLI option.
  - HMAC key files contain exactly 32 raw bytes, binary, no hex/base64/newline.
  - Accept inactive keys only during rotation window; new tokens use active_hmac_key_id.
  - Token request flow: read Authorization Bearer, reject missing/malformed, hash token, look up active row, reject revoked/expired, load mcp_users, attach user context.
  - Do not accept tokens in URLs by default.
- JOPLIN-MCP-RUST.md:678-699 defines mcp_tokens schema fields.
- JOPLIN-MCP-RUST.md:1789-1809 defines token storage and server stores only token hashes.

Scope:
- Implement raw token generation with secure randomness.
- Implement HMAC-SHA256 hashing with configured 32-byte key.
- Implement key loading and strict key length validation.
- Implement key id storage and active/inactive key lookup for validation.
- Implement token insert, check, revoke, expiry, last_seen_at behavior without per-request write storms if possible.
- Implement Authorization Bearer parsing and user context attachment.
- Implement token revocation endpoint backend behavior.

Out of scope:
- Client token file storage belongs to client issue.
- Bootstrap Joplin auth belongs to Joplin auth issue.
- OAuth 2.1 is explicitly not in v1.

Desired outcome:
The MCP server owns safe read-only credentials independent of Joplin sessions.

Verification:
- Unit tests reject raw-token lookup and ensure raw tokens are never stored.
- Unit tests reject HMAC key files not exactly 32 raw bytes.
- Token lookup rejects missing, malformed, unknown, revoked, and expired tokens.
- New tokens use active_hmac_key_id.
- Existing tokens can validate against configured inactive key during rotation window if implemented.
- Revocation records revoked_at, revoked_by/reason/from_ip when available.
- Logs never include raw token, token hash, or full Authorization header.

description:
Problem statement:

Source of truth:
- JOPLIN-MCP-RUST.md:1-10 defines plan version, date, MCP spec target 2025-06-18, and RFC 2119 normative language.
- JOPLIN-MCP-RUST.md:11-20 defines purpose: LAN-only Rust MCP system for LLM read access to unencrypted Joplin Server notes, avoiding one Docker container per user, avoiding static per-user credentials in Nix, and replacing an upstream Python MCP image.
- JOPLIN-MCP-RUST.md:22-76 defines hard limitations and non-goals: unencrypted only, read-only first, owner items only, LAN-only, no shared notebook access, no resource binary download, no direct mutation of Joplin tables.
- JOPLIN-MCP-RUST.md:2055-2090 defines project acceptance criteria.

Global constraints every child issue must preserve:
- No Joplin E2EE decryption, no E2EE passwords, no master-key handling.
- No write tools and no direct writes to canonical Joplin tables.
- Owner-only visibility: index items owned by the authenticated Joplin user only. Shared notebooks are unsupported in v1 and must not be inferred from shares. If the owner shares a folder, owner-owned items remain indexable for the owner; recipient/shared-only visibility is out of scope.
- LAN-only reachability is not the security model; TLS, Origin validation, auth, token hashing, redaction, and fail-early checks still apply.
- Raw MCP tokens and Joplin passwords must never be stored or logged.
- Direct Joplin DB reads must be isolated behind a source trait so future API-source work can be added without contaminating tool or auth code.

Desired outcome:
A working Rust workspace with `joplin-mcpd` and `joplin-mcp-client`, migrations, bootstrap auth, token issuance/revocation, read-only indexing, MCP tools, observability, tests, and Nix/LXC deployment support matching the plan.

Verification summary:
- Milestone 1 local proof passes without real Joplin Server.
- Milestone 2 real Joplin integration passes using test-only SOPS secrets without logging values.
- Milestone 3 LLM harness usability passes.
- Acceptance criteria in JOPLIN-MCP-RUST.md:2055-2090 are satisfied.

Parallelization notes:
Phase epics split work by subsystem. Most implementation tasks can run in parallel once shared schema/config contracts exist.
